content.text:
Notely now sends a welcome email when a user is created and a password reset email on request, through **Resend**. Lint passes. I ran a quick test without an API key, where emails print to the console instead of sending: signup sent the welcome email, a reset for an unknown address sent nothing, and a reset link worked once and was rejected the second time. No email has been sent through Resend yet, since the key is a placeholder.

**Why Resend:** it's built for Next.js and has a simple API. I call it with plain `fetch`, so there's no new package.

**Changes:**
- **`src/lib/email.ts`** (new): sends the email through Resend and holds both email templates. Each email has an HTML and a plain-text version, and names are escaped in the HTML. Without `RESEND_API_KEY`, emails print to the server console in development, and sending fails with an error in production.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`**:
  - **`createUser({ email, name })`**: this didn't exist before, so I added it. It rejects duplicate emails, then sends the welcome email. If the email fails, the error is logged but the account is still created.
  - **`requestPasswordReset(email)`**: creates a random reset token that expires after 30 minutes and emails a link to `/reset-password?token=…`. Only a hash of the token is stored. A new request cancels any earlier link. It behaves the same for unknown addresses, so it can't be used to check which emails have accounts.
  - **`consumePasswordResetToken(token)`**: checks the token and returns the user, and each token works only once.
- **`.env.example`**: placeholder `RESEND_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM` and `APP_URL`. The existing `.gitignore` rule `.env*` would have excluded this file, so I added `!.env.example`.

**Still missing:**
- Users have no passwords in the app yet, so `consumePasswordResetToken` confirms the user but doesn't set a new password. Saving it is one line once passwords are stored.
- There's no `/reset-password` page or signup form yet. Nothing in the app calls the new functions; they're ready to use from server actions.
- Users and reset tokens are kept in memory, the same way the existing users are, so they reset when the server restarts.
- To send real email: verify your domain in Resend, then set `RESEND_API_KEY` and `EMAIL_FROM` to an address on that domain.

`tsc` reports one error, a missing `LayoutProps` type in `layout.tsx`. That file is unchanged; Next generates the type during a build. I haven't committed anything.
